items.title: Morning Briefing: Nov. 4, 2026
items.excerpt: Here’s a rundown of all the news you need to start your Wednesday, including US Democrats projected to win both houses of Congress in midterm elections, US midterms delivering wave of historic firsts across states, and President Donald Trump’s pledging to end US financial aid to Israel by year’s end. Democrats were projected to take control of both chambers of the US Congress in Tuesday's midterm elections, delivering a major political setback to President Donald Trump and his Republican Party, according to US media projections. The party made significant gains beyond its traditional strongholds, winning key races in states that overwhelmingly supported Trump in the 2024 presidential election, including Texas, South Carolina, Ohio, Iowa, and Kansas. The scale of the Democratic wave was still becoming clear early Wednesday, but the results pointed to widespread voter dissatisfaction with the Trump administration, particularly over the economy, rising living costs, and the president's decision to launch a war against Iran in February. - US midterms deliver wave of historic firsts across states, Congress Tuesday’s US midterm elections produced a series of historic firsts in races for governor, Senate and the House of Representatives. In Georgia, Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms became the first Black woman elected governor of any US state, as well as Georgia’s first woman and first Black governor. Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland won in New Mexico to become the first Native American woman elected governor in US history, while Minnesota Democrat Peggy Flanagan became the first Native American woman elected to the US Senate. In New Jersey, Democrat Adam Hamawy won the 12th Congressional District to become the state’s first Muslim member of Congress. Texas Democrat Gina Hinojosa became the state’s first Latina governor, while Republican Byron Donalds was elected Florida’s first Black governor. In Ohio, Amy Acton became the state’s first woman and first Jewish governor, while David Crowley became Wisconsin’s first Black governor. Illinois Democrat Juliana Stratton’s Senate victory also means three Black women will serve simultaneously in the chamber for the first time. - Trump pledges end to US aid for Israel by year’s end US President Donald Trump said Tuesday that Washington will stop providing financial aid to Israel by year's end under an agreement reached with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. "Netanyahu and I have made a deal that we give Israel $4 billion a year, and we made a deal months ago that we're stopping, and they're fine with it because, you know, they've become a very successful country that are not in need, and we won't be paying any more to Israel," Trump told Fox News. He added that Washington would still provide assistance if needed, describing Israel as a regional partner with whom the US has maintained "a tremendous relationship," with Tel Aviv being the smaller partner.

items.excerpt: ## Voters Deliver Stunning Rebuke of Trump with Democrats Regaining Control of Congress Nov 04, 2026 In a stunning repudiation of President Trump and his MAGA movement, Democrats regained control of the House and the Senate in Tuesday’s midterm elections. Democrats have picked up at least seven Senate seats, winning races in Texas, Maine, Ohio, South Carolina, North Carolina, Iowa and Kansas, as well as winning in Michigan. The Senate races in Mississippi and Alaska remain too close to call. In the House, Democrats have won at least 231 seats, with more races still to be decided. Only twice in the last half-century has control of both chambers changed hands in the same election. Democrats also clinched a majority of governorships. ## Historic Night in Texas as Democrats Win Senate Seat and Governorship ... In Texas, Democrats have shattered more than three decades of Republican dominance, winning races for U.S. Sen ... James Talarico will be the first Democrat to represent Texas in the U.S. Senate since Lloyd Bentsen left in 1993. ... Meanwhile, Texas Republican Governor Greg Abbott has lost his bid for a fourth term. Democratic state Representative Gina Hinojosa defeated Abbott by nearly 700,000 votes. She becomes Texas’s first-ever Latina governor.

items.title: US Services Sector Activity Cools Slightly in October; Inflation Remains Elevated
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Nov 4 (Reuters) - US services sector growth slowed marginally in ⁠October ⁠amid a moderation in new ⁠orders, but supply chains remained strained, keeping prices for inputs elevated. The Institute for ​Supply Management said on Wednesday its nonmanufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index dipped to 54.5 last month from 54.9 in September. A ‌reading above 50 indicates growth in ‌the services sector, which accounts for more than two-thirds of US economic activity. Economists polled by Reuters ⁠had forecast the ⁠PMI little changed at 54.8. The PMI suggested the economy started the fourth quarter ​on solid footing, though economists expect a slowdown in activity, with consumer spending expected to pull back after back-to-back quarters of robust growth. Spending is seen in part curbed by high inflation, which is eroding household purchasing power. Income at the ​disposal of households, after adjusting for inflation and taxes, fell in September after being unchanged in ⁠August.

A wave of anger over ​Trump's policies, particularly the US-Iran war's role in pushing the cost of living higher, helped Democrats take the Senate, where they flipped seats in deeply Republican states for a majority of at least 54-44, and the House of Representatives, where they gained ‌at least 25 seats. It will be the first time that Trump, a Republican who also held the White House from 2017 to 2021, has had to contend with a Democratic-controlled Congress. Alia Bhatt and Neetu Kapoor were among the first to arrive, showing their support for Ranbir Kapoor, who essays the role of Lord Rama in the film.

Movie Review: In ‘Wild Horse Nine,’ death looms for a CIA goon John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell play a couple of bickering CIA agents on a trip to Easter Island in Martin McDonagh's “Wild Horse Nine.” The dark comedy is set in 1973, just before the military coup in Chile, and Malkovich's character is getting a little loose lipped about the plans. In her review for The Associated Press, film writer Lindsey Bahr writes that while the territory and themes may be familiar for McDonagh, the actors elevate even the less savory clunkers. “Wild Horse Nine” is rated R and is playing in theaters starting Friday. LONDON (AP) — Jurors have started deliberating in Russell Brand's trial on charges of rape and sexual assault. After three weeks of evidence, the judge at London’s Southwark Crown Court instructed the jury to reach a unanimous decision. Brand, who is free on bail, has attended court daily with his wife. Six women accuse him of sexual misconduct between 1999 and 2009. Prosecutors claim Brand was a "sexual predator" during that time. Brand, 51, has pleaded not guilty, stating his encounters were consensual. His lawyer argued the claims were influenced by a 2023 documentary. Brand rose to fame in the early 2000s and now has a large online following. The new animated “The Cat in the Hat” has plenty of tricks up its sleeve, says Associated Press critic Mark Kennedy. Directed by Erica Rivinoja and Alessandro Carloni, the film takes a Marvel-style approach, with world-saving stakes and a mysterious villain. Bill Hader voices the Cat, who works for a corporate conglomerate tasked with cheering up kids. The film features stylized animation and a star-studded voice cast, including Giancarlo Esposito and Bowen Yang. Despite its whimsical source material, the movie's messaging feels muddled, and the plot is overloaded with Things. It hits theaters Friday and is rated PG. ... NEW YORK (AP) — Tony Butala, co-founder of the Grammy-nominated trio The Lettermen, has died at age 87. The band's media coordinator confirmed his death and shared a statement from the band expressing deep sadness and sending condolences to his family and friends. Butala died Sunday. Butala's career began in childhood, singing professionally by age 7. In the late ‘50s, he co-founded The Lettermen with Jim Pike and Bob Engemann. They became one of the most popular vocal groups of the 1960s, with hits like “The Way You Look Tonight” and “When I Fall in Love.” Butala was the last surviving member of the trio’s original lineup. In 2020, Butala and The Lettermen received a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame. Even Godzilla can be felled by an old hazard: the sophomore slump. Though Godzilla has been stomping around for more than half a century, “Godzilla Minus Zero” is a sequel. It follows the quite excellent, Oscar-winning “Godzilla Minus One,” a reset for the kaiju franchise that brought Godzilla back to its postwar Japan roots. Like its predecessor, the follow-up marries human-scaled drama with a flair for stompy-stomp spectacle. Yet AP Film Writer Jake Coyle says those calibrations are slightly off in “Godzilla Minus Zero.” In his review, Coyle writes that the melodrama on the ground overtakes the movie, sagging it with a bloated story that leaves you pining for the big guy to turn up again. NEW YORK (AP) — David Mendizábal is directing a revival of Lin-Manuel Miranda’s "In the Heights," a musical that was Mendizábal's introduction to theater. The show, running for three weeks at New York City Center, features a new cast of Latino artists. Mendizábal emphasizes the importance of showcasing Latino communities, especially now. Miranda, who starred in the original production, reflects on the musical's enduring relevance. The revival comes amid immigration tensions, highlighting themes of gentrification and community. New and old cast members say the musical remains a celebration of the Latino immigrant experience, with its messages resonating strongly today. NEW YORK (AP) — My Chemical Romance has hit No. 1 on the Billboard 200 with “The Black Parade (20th Anniversary Deluxe Edition).” This reissue of their 2006 rock opera includes six bonus tracks. Back then, it debuted at No. 2 due to competition from Disney’s “Hannah Montana” soundtrack. The reissue's success is driven by 20 physical variants and a significant increase in album sales. The band’s reunion and anniversary tour have also fueled interest. Nostalgic fans and new listeners are connecting with the album's unique style and themes. This marks the longest wait for an album to reach No. 1. WASHINGTON (AP) — The Kennedy Center has announced that Paul Anka, David Foster, Andy Garcia, David Mamet and Barbara Mandrell will be honored at this year's Kennedy Center Honors. The event will take place away from the iconic venue for the first time due to President Donald Trump's legal battle over renovations and naming rights. The nominees have had substantial careers in their fields. Mamet is a renowned playwright, while Mandrell is a Country Music Hall of Fame member. Anka, a longtime friend of Trump, has rewritten “My Way” with MAGA-themed lyrics. The ceremony will be held on December 7 at Washington's Capital One Arena.
